subject: Improper Posterior detected - techniques for debugging?

messages.author: 54788cf3a8eb8916
messages.subject: Improper Posterior detected - techniques for debugging?
parts:
Hi folks,

I have just written a new hierarchical model version of the banana distribution - i.e. the Goel-Okumoto model for software bugs.  I have specified ranges for every parameter - which I think is valid, however I am getting the message

Posterior is improper. Please check your model.
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done

What general techniques can I use for pinning down the source of my error?

If the model has detected a variable out of range, would it be possible to print the name of this variable and moan about it specifically to help in debugging?

Kind regards,

Sean O'Riordain
Trinity College,
Dublin

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Improper Posterior detected - techniques for debugging?
parts:
On 11/12/13, 3:23 AM, Sean O'Riordain wrote:
> Hi folks,
>
> I have just written a new hierarchical model version of the banana distribution - i.e. the Goel-Okumoto model for
> software bugs. I have specified ranges for every parameter - which I think is valid, however I am getting the message

You can also get problems with overflow or underflow
or boundary conditions in functions (like 0 / 0).

> Posterior is improper. Please check your model.
> error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done
>
> What general techniques can I use for pinning down the source of my error?

Print results as you go along.

Start with simpler models and build up. For example,
build the non-hierarchical version first.

If we had better debuggers, we might not need to
recommend the first option --- but the second's probably
good practice for any model-building exercise.

> If the model has detected a variable out of range, would it be possible to print the name of this variable and moan
> about it specifically to help in debugging?

We've been debating how much to intervene with error
handling.

Right now, we only do thorough checking on the distribution
functions and some of the other non-built-in functions.

Whatever we do, if we want to get down to checking
every function including arithmetic operators and
C++ lib functions like log() and exp(), then we're going to
need a way to turn it off so there's not too big an efficiency
hit. Error checking may seem cheap, but all those branches
can hurt both inlining at compile time and branch prediction at
run time.

It's in our sights, but not coming in the very near future.

- Bob

Thanks Bob,

Using the print() function inside in the for loop of the model{} to print out all the little pieces of the model as it goes by highlighted an error in the scale of one of my parameters and I adjusted the supports for my variables.

Kind regards,
Sean
